subject: Renewal term adaptation + QBR slotting for CloudNova
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lowe <jordan.lowe@cloudnova.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal term adaptation + QBR slotting for CloudNova

Jordan —

Thanks again for the time last week. As CloudNova’s usage profile has grown, we want to get ahead of the upcoming renewal and make sure the new term covers the burst/seasonal capacity you expect next year. Proposed goals for this thread:

- Align on a preferred contract term (12 vs 24 months) and an uplift runway for seasonal bursts.
- Lock a QBR window in Oct/Nov to review capacity/SLAs and the technical runbook.
- Identify the minimal procurement checklist for legal/finance so we can avoid delays.

Quick proposal from our side: 24-month term with a stepped capacity ladder (baseline + two scheduled burst windows) to keep unit pricing predictable. I attached a short term scenarios overview and your July MAU snapshot so we can model pricing.

Can you share 2–3 dates in Oct/early Nov that work for your exec + infra leads? Once you give times, I’ll send a calendar hold and loop in Lauren (success) and Priyom (solutions) to map the QBR agenda.

Thanks —
Michael

Michael Grant
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
micah.grant@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Renewal_Term_Scenarios_v2.pdf (summary of 12/24m scenarios; pricing delta table) ; CloudNova_MAU_report_Jul2026.csv (usage by route)
From: Jordan Lowe <jordan.lowe@cloudnova.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@cloudnova.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T13:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal term adaptation + QBR slotting for CloudNova

Hi Michael —

Appreciate the clear options. Short answers:

- We lean toward 24 months if we can get predictable burst pricing for the holiday windows (Nov–Dec and Mar).
- For QBRs, our exec + infra availability is best: Oct 20–22 (mornings PT) or Nov 9–11 (afternoons PT).
- Procurement will need an SOW-level estimate for peak RPU and a short note on data residency (we run EU tenants too).

I attached a quick internal note on expected peak routes. Can Lauren/Priyom confirm the burst planning cadence and whether the stepped burst model can be automated via Redwood’s Dedicated capacity?

Jordan

Jordan Lowe
Head of Platform, CloudNova
jordan.lowe@cloudnova.com | +1 512-555-8890

Attachment: CloudNova_peak_routes_Aug2026.xlsx

Thanks — adding a few operational notes before we lock dates:

- Dedicated capacity: yes, we can automate stepped bursts with scheduled policies. I estimate 48–72 hours lead-time for capacity warm-up per burst depending on GPU family.
- Pricing: stepped-burst model can be a blended effective rate; I’ll draft 2 example ladders (conservative/aggressive) by EOD.
- Data residency: Naomi will confirm EU tenancy mapping and whether we need an addendum for cross-region mirroring.

Action items for our calendar invite:
- QBR agenda (30/60/90 day runbook, staffing/readout owners, escalation path).
- Legal/finance delegates to attend or pre-review the SOW wording.

I suggest we propose Oct 21 (09:30 PT) or Nov 10 (14:00 PT) to Jordan — they gave good windows. Michael, want me to send the invite with the two proposed options?

—Priyom

Thanks all — looking forward to the QBR.
